conviction_note: The fundamental read is a beat: four straight quarters landed 6-10% above the guide, which puts Q3 near $236-244M against a $225-229M consensus. The reaction read is close to a coin flip leaning down: the stock is at an all-time high, up 19% in 20 days and above the consensus target, put skew is +5.6 vol points, and the last print after a run-up (Aug 2026) bought only +1.7% on a 5.6% beat over a raised guide. The Q3 2025 print, which carried a decelerating Q4 guide, fell 15%. So p_up is 48 on a 13.5% move (-0.54), and the findings sum to -2.0 because the positioning and guidance-decel findings carry more weight than the expected beat.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue. Company guide $223-225M (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026052558/hnge-q2202684xex991.htm, 2026-08-04). Street consensus $229.05M per Chartmill (snippet; the page returned 403 on fetch) and about $225M per a Tickeron preview dated 2026-10-25, both seen in search snippets. Two estimate sources within about 2% of each other, both at or above the top of the guide. EPS consensus disagrees ($0.58-0.61 non-GAAP) and is not used. The implied Q4 bar comes from the FY guide of $856-860M: 858 - 182.3 - 212.8 - 224 = about $239M, +40% y/y on Q4 2025's $170.7M.
positioning_check: Short interest 6,309,855 shares, 9.64% of float, 3.6 days to cover, as of the 2026-10-15 settlement (FINRA, published 2026-10-26), down 0.35% from 6,332,267 on 2026-09-30, per https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/HNGE/short-interest/ and https://equibles.com/stocks/hnge/shortinterest. Elevated but not a crowded short (below the 18-23% that squeezed in past runs). Options: 25d skew +5.57 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 3.14, event-implied move 13.34% (straddle 15.07%). Tape: spot $117.44 at a 52-week and all-time high, +5.1% over 5 days, +19.4% over 20 days, +277% off the 52-week low. Insiders sold 1,024,581 shares ($95.6M) in 90 days under 10b5-1 plans; 23 Form 144s were filed from 2026-08-28 to 2026-10-14.

findings.finding: Hinge has beaten its own revenue guide by 6-10% for four straight quarters: Q4 2025 $170.7M vs a $155-157M guide (+9.5%), Q1 2026 $182.3M vs $171-173M (+6.0%), and Q2 2026 $212.8M vs $194-196M original (+9.1%) and $200-202M raised (+5.9%). The same beat on the Q3 guide of $223-225M gives about $236-244M, 3-7% above the $225-229M consensus, with a FY raise from $856-860M likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026 (Q4 beat 9.5% plus a FY guide) +17.3%; May 2026 (Q1 beat 6%) +10.2%; Aug 2026 (Q2 beat 5.9% over the raised guide, FY raised $37M at the midpoint) only +1.7% close to close after a July run to a high; Nov 2025 (Q3 beat) -15.1%. The beat itself is bought only when the stock has not run into it.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus at $229M already sits above the top of the guide, so the street models part of the pattern. What would be unpriced is a beat in line with the history ($236M+), which consensus does not carry. If the full pattern were priced, consensus would be $236M+, and the 17% October run-up may already embed that whisper.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 beat: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1673743/000162828026006826/hnge-2026210xex991.htm. Q1 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026030499/hnge-q1202655xex991.htm. The June 9 pre-raise shows the same yield/conversion driver mid-quarter: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001673743/000162828026041886/hnge-202669ex991.htm. All three are company documents, consistent with each other.

findings.finding: The sell-side raised targets aggressively into the print and the stock overshot them. KeyBanc went to $140 from $125 ahead of Q3 (~2026-10-16), BofA to $130 from $110 (~10-23), Stifel to $130 from $115 (~10-26), and AAII counts 3 upgrades and 0 downgrades in the month to 10-30. The stock rose 17% in October to $117, above the $108-114 consensus target. The bar for the reaction is a beat-and-raise well above the guide, not the guide itself.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Aug 2026: the stock ran to a 52-week high after the July 13 Morgan Stanley and Barclays raises, then a 5.9% beat over the raised guide plus a FY raise closed only +1.7% (up 9.5% intraday). Feb and May 2026, without a comparable pre-print run, gained +17% and +10%.
findings.source_date: 2026-11-02 snapshot (relative ages: KeyBanc 17 days, BofA 10 days, Stifel 7 days)
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so it is not unpriced information. It says the stock already carries the expected beat. Positive skew (+5.6) and put/call OI of 3.14 show hedgers agree. A market that had not priced the beat would show the stock below targets and calls bid.
findings.independence: AAII 2026-11-02 (3 upgrades, 0 downgrades in the month; +17.1% in October): https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/541632-why-hinge-health-inc8217s-hnge-stock-is-up-521. MarketBeat 2026-10-26 (new high $113.48, consensus target $108): https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/price-hinge-health-nyse-hnge-reaches-new-52-week-high-should-you-buy-2026-10-26/. The baseline skew is a separate source.

findings.finding: The FY 2026 guide of $856-860M implies Q4 revenue of about $239M, +40% y/y on $170.7M, against +45% guided for Q3 and +53% printed in Q2. The first Q4 guide given at this print will likely show headline deceleration, and the call is where 2027 client-launch visibility (the January 1 cohort) gets its first read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (2025-11-04) beat and raised FY 2025 to $572-574M, but its Q4 guide of $155-157M implied +33% growth against +53% printed, and the stock fell 15.1% (a lock-up expiring 2025-11-17 contributed). That is the same seasonal print as this one.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, because guide conservatism is now well known (each guide was beaten by 6-10%). The arithmetic Q4 decel is visible to anyone, but consensus revenue revisions (+7.75% over three months per Chartmill) suggest the street models continued 45%+ growth. If the decel were priced, skew would be heavier and targets would not have risen in October.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 release with the Q4 2025 decel guide: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251103237172/en/Hinge-Health-reports-third-quarter-2025-financial-results. The Q3 2026 implied figure uses the same Q2 2026 document as finding 1 (the same document read for a different line).

findings.finding: The Q3 non-GAAP operating margin guide steps down to 28% at the midpoint ($61-63M on $224M) from 29% printed in Q2. Management is investing in GI (the $105M cash Cylinder Health acquisition, expected to close in Q3 with a 2027 program launch) and migraine, analysts flagged these as slowing margin expansion, and the release does not say whether guidance includes Cylinder.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on margin; operating income has beaten every quarter (Q2 $61.5M vs a $50-52M guide).
findings.why_not_priced: Small and mostly known. It matters only if Cylinder costs or new-program spend show up in the Q4 or FY operating-income guide while revenue upside is smaller than usual.
findings.independence: Zacks note that higher GI and migraine investment could slow margin expansion: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3018950/reasons-to-hold-hinge-health-stock-in-your-portfolio-for-now. This shares the Q2 document with findings 1 and 3.

findings.finding: Insiders and pre-IPO holders keep supplying stock: 1,024,581 shares ($95.6M) sold in 90 days and 23 Form 144s filed from 2026-08-28 to 2026-10-14 (the CFO sold 55,561 shares at $89.45 on 9-10 and the President 33,000 at $88.05 on 8-21, both under 10b5-1 plans). There is an ongoing overhang into any post-print strength.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 print fell 15% two weeks before a 77M-share lock-up expiry. No comparable cliff sits in this window.
findings.why_not_priced: These are routine, pre-scheduled 10b5-1 sales and the market has absorbed them while rising 19%. They matter only as a cap on follow-through.

findings.finding: Short interest is 9.64% of float (6.31M shares, 3.6 days to cover, as of 2026-10-15) and roughly flat since a 1.5M-share build into the 9-30 settlement. That is enough to add a short-covering leg if the print clears the elevated bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest peaked at 6.7M (2026-07-15) ahead of the Aug print, which closed only +1.7%, so covering did not show up as a large move then.
findings.why_not_priced: Conditional mechanism: it adds to the upside only on a clean beat. It is not crowded enough to make a squeeze the base case.
findings.independence: Equibles, the same FINRA data, a model forecast of 6.03M for 10-30 and a squeeze score of 77/100: https://equibles.com/stocks/hnge/shortinterest

findings.finding: There is $300.0M of buyback authorization available after the July 29, 2026 increase (about 3.3% of the $9.2B market cap), against Q2 free cash flow of $99.6M and $475.6M of cash. An accelerated pace or a new increase is possible at the print.

findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is known. Only a further increase would be new, and at a P/E near 88 a buyback is a small support.

rejected_candidates.detail: The sealed baseline tape and MarketBeat both put the stock at $107-117 in late October; the article contradicts itself.
It conflicts with the $0.58-0.61 non-GAAP figures from Chartmill and Tickeron and is likely a GAAP or stale basis; not used as the bar.

baseline_tension: The evidence agrees with the skew and cuts against the run-up. The fundamentals point to another beat, but the stock is at an all-time high above consensus targets after a 19% 20-day run, and options pay for downside (+5.6 skew, put/call OI 3.14). The lean is therefore slightly negative and close to a coin flip, not a fade with conviction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-pattern finding went from +1.5 to +1.0, because the Aug 2026 print bought only +1.7% on a comparable beat after a run-up
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct went from 12.5 to 13.5, toward the 13.34% implied move and the 15% median reaction; p_up stays at 48, so expected_move_pct goes from -0.50 to -0.54

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was checked (9.6% of float, 3.6 DTC; not crowded) and the negatives agree with the positive skew, so no negative was shrunk; the short-interest finding stays at +0.5
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced to the company guide plus two estimate sources within about 2%, so no cap applies
